purpose: Sevelamer carbonate is used to control high phosphorus levels in your blood if you have chronic kidney disease and are on dialysis. When your kidneys are not working well, phosphorus can build up in your body. Too much phosphorus can weaken your bones and harm your heart and blood vessels.
how_it_works: This medicine works inside your stomach and intestines, not in your bloodstream. It acts like a sponge that grabs onto phosphorus from the food you eat and traps it. The trapped phosphorus then passes out of your body in your stool instead of being absorbed into your blood.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects are stomach-related, such as nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, diarrhea, or constipation. These are usually mild and may improve over time. Taking it with meals can help reduce stomach upset.
warnings: Tell your doctor if you have trouble swallowing, a bowel blockage, or major stomach surgery, as this medicine may not be safe for you. Sevelamer can interfere with the absorption of certain other medications, so always take your other medicines at least 1 hour before or 3 hours after sevelamer. Do not crush or chew the tablets — swallow them whole.
typical_dosing: This medicine is taken by mouth with each meal, usually 3 times a day. Your doctor will decide the exact dose based on your phosphorus levels. It comes as a tablet or powder mixed with water. Always take it at the start of your meal as directed by your doctor or pharmacist.
